intro: The bridge to the Number Gate has fallen into pieces. Only fair shares can rebuild it!
To fix it, we need to really learn about Fractions Are Fair Shares.
Study at each place, talk to my friends, and explain what you learn!
story.goal: Learn the three big ideas of Fractions Are Fair Shares to wake The Number Gate.
story.finale: You remembered it all! The Number Gate shines again thanks to you.

companion.name: Pip
companion.greeting: Hi, I'm Pip! I'll help you if you get stuck. Let's explore!

zones.name: Wizard's Tower
zones.description: A place to learn about what is a fraction.

zones.description: A place to learn about top and bottom numbers.

zones.name: Market Fountain
zones.description: A place to learn about comparing fractions.

zones.name: The Number Gate
zones.description: It wakes up when you master Fractions Are Fair Shares.

npcs.name: Merla
npcs.title: the Number Wizard
npcs.persona: Playful wizard who treats numbers like magic spells. Teaches "What Is a Fraction" from the lesson "Fractions Are Fair Shares".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Merla. Want to learn about fraction with me?
teach: When you cut a pizza into equal pieces, each piece is a fraction of the pizza.
The pieces must be the same size for the fraction to be fair.
A fraction shows a part of a whole.

npcs.title: the Knight
npcs.persona: Honourable, encouraging knight who loves fair play. Teaches "Top and Bottom Numbers" from the lesson "Fractions Are Fair Shares".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Sir Digit. Want to learn about fraction with me?
teach: It tells how many equal parts the whole is split into.
The bottom number is the denominator.
knowledge: The bottom number is the denominator.
It tells how many equal parts the whole is split into.
The top number is the numerator.
It tells how many of those parts you have.
In 3/4, you have three parts out of four.

npcs.name: Penny
npcs.title: the Merchant
npcs.persona: Chatty market trader who explains with everyday shopping examples. Teaches "Comparing Fractions" from the lesson "Fractions Are Fair Shares".
npcs.greeting: Hello there! I'm Penny. Want to learn about bigger with me?
teach: When two fractions have the same denominator, the one with the bigger numerator is bigger.
When the numerators are both 1, the fraction with the smaller denominator is bigger, because the whole is cut into fewer, larger pieces.
